h: Shows, Galleries and a Bit of Bowling
p: Victoria is something of a theatre hotspot. The Apollo Victoria and the Victoria Palace Theatre sit right by the station, so a matinee followed by an evening on the lanes, or a few frames before a show, is a very easy double bill. Book both well in advance if you're aiming for a weekend.

Art lovers can head south towards the river to Tate Britain on Millbank, home to centuries of British art and free to enter for the main collection. It's a pleasant walk from Victoria, and once you're there, the riverside views along the Thames are a bonus. Back towards the station, the shops and restaurants around Nova and Cardinal Place make a handy pit stop for a bite before or after your game.

As for the game itself, a bit of know-how helps. Pick a ball that fits your hand and that you can swing smoothly. Aim for the arrows on the lane rather than the pins, keep your release smooth and follow through. Don't step over the foul line, as that cancels the shot. The scoring screen handles the maths, so all you need to do is celebrate.
Victoria is very well connected, with the Tube, mainline trains and the coach station nearby. For groups travelling from different parts of London, it's one of the easiest places to meet.
